findings.quote: Our view: margins are improving for real, but the growth in GAAP earnings is not as fast as the adjusted figures suggest.
findings.issue: The release contradicts this for the quarter the paragraph discusses. GAAP net income rose 41% and GAAP diluted EPS rose 39%. Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Income went from $11.1 million to $14.6 million and Adjusted Diluted EPS rose 32%. The release says outright: "The percentage increase in GAAP Net Income exceeded Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Income." The same paragraph's "the gap is mostly stock compensation" also lacks support. The Adjusted Net Income reconciliation is cut off in the excerpt, and the stock compensation line appears only in the EBITDA reconciliation, before tax.
findings.fix: Drop the conclusion or reverse it. The supportable claim is that the gap between GAAP and adjusted EPS is widening in dollars as stock compensation grows ($5,272k against $3,512k in the EBITDA reconciliation). GAAP growth outpaced adjusted growth this quarter, partly because the prior-year quarter carried business realignment expenses that did not recur. Remove "mostly" unless a figure on the surface supports it.

findings.quote: The trailing multiple is high because FY25 GAAP EPS of $0.87 still reflects lower margins
findings.issue: Wrong period. The 42.4x P/E (TTM) is on trailing-twelve-month earnings. $43.23 / $0.87 is about 50x, not 42.4x, so the multiple is not built on FY25 EPS. The sentence attaches the TTM multiple to the FY25 figure.
findings.fix: Explain the trailing multiple with TTM figures, for example the 9.0% TTM operating margin against the 10.9% latest-quarter margin. Or drop the FY25 EPS figure from this sentence.

findings.quote: the stock trades near the top of its 52-week range and above the forward multiples a slower-growing marketplace would usually earn
findings.issue: No benchmark multiple is on the surface. The Facts block's Multiples heading says "peers pending a peer data source", so a "usual" multiple for a slower-growing marketplace is recalled or invented. The same unsupported comparison recurs in sections.risks.systemic: "The stock also trades at a premium multiple" (premium to what?).
findings.fix: Argue valuation from the company's own figures: 26.2x NTM against the TTM P/E of 42.4x, the 52-week range and the $50.00–$52.00 Street band. Drop "premium" and "would usually earn", or say no peer set was captured.

findings.quote: The 10-K flags dependence on Amazon.com, Inc. as an RSCG inventory vendor; see Risks.
findings.issue: Over-attribution. The 10-K excerpt names the Amazon vendor contracts but never ties them to RSCG or any other segment. The link is an inference the source invites but does not make. The same attachment appears in four more places: thesis.body ("the RSCG segment depends partly on inventory bought from Amazon"), businessMoat.durability ("the RSCG segment relies in part on a single large vendor"), risks.idiosyncratic[0] ("This sits inside RSCG, the segment that drove most of the quarter's profit gain") and valuation.scenarios[2].driver ("RSCG loses Amazon inventory"). In idiosyncratic[0], "most of the quarter's profit gain" also stands in for segment direct profit, which is a different quantity.
findings.fix: Attribute only what the 10-K says: the company buys inventory from Amazon.com, Inc. under vendor contracts and likely could not replace it quickly. If you link it to RSCG, frame it as your inference (RSCG is the purchase-model, consumer-goods segment). Say "segment direct profit" where that is the figure meant.

findings.quote: More sales from fewer bidders can reflect better matching, but it can also mean the buyer pool is thinning
findings.issue: Misreads the metric. The release defines auction participants per auction: "a registered buyer who bids in more than one auction is counted as an auction participant in each auction in which he or she bids." A 5% drop does not show fewer bidders or a thinning pool, because registered buyers rose 9% over the same period. With completed transactions up 17%, the figures point to fewer bids per auction, not fewer buyers. The same misreading shapes risks.idiosyncratic[1] ("sellers could see weaker recovery") and moatFactors[0].
findings.fix: State the definition once and read the two counts together. Participant-auction pairs fell while auctions rose, so participation per auction thinned. Whether unique buyers fell is not on the surface. Keep the risk, but frame it as bid density, not buyer count.

findings.quote: Stock compensation is rising, per the reconciliation, so buybacks partly offset dilution rather than shrinking the share count.
findings.issue: Causal claim the pack does not establish. No share-count series is on the surface: only 31.33M derived from market cap, and the 33.0 million diluted weighted shares expected for the fiscal fourth quarter. Rising stock compensation expense alone does not show whether the count is rising or falling net of the $16.2M FY25 repurchases.
findings.fix: Say that stock compensation expense rose ($5,272k against $3,512k in the quarter) and that the pack does not show the net share-count trend. Or drop the conclusion about offsetting dilution.

findings.quote: These sellers tend to stay once their disposal processes run through a platform
findings.issue: Unsupported claim. No retention, churn or tenure figure for GovDeals sellers is on the surface. The release cites "seller acquisition" and "continued marketplace adoption", not retention.
findings.fix: Ground the factor in what the release shows: GovDeals GMV up 9%, direct profit up 9%, a 95% direct-profit ratio, and seller acquisition cited as a driver. Present stickiness as your judgment, not a fact, or cut it.

findings.quote: A lower gross margin is not by itself a warning sign here: the filings do not explain the full five-year decline, but a purchase-model sale books the whole price as revenue while a consignment sale books only the fee, so mix moves the ratio.
findings.issue: The mechanism cuts against the thesis and the paragraph does not say so. Fee revenue carries a high direct-profit ratio, so a falling gross margin points to a rising purchase-model share of revenue, not a consignment shift. The FY25 drop to 43.8% came alongside +31.2% revenue growth. The paragraph cites mix to dismiss the decline when, on its own logic, mix explains it in the bearish direction.
findings.fix: Name the counter-case. On this mechanism the FY21–FY25 gross-margin decline points to more purchase-model revenue, which sits awkwardly with the consignment-led margin story. The quarterly consignment share (83.1% against 82.5%) is the evidence that the mix has since turned.

findings.quote: Profit is growing faster than volume because more of the business runs through consignment, where the company earns a fee rather than reselling inventory.
findings.issue: Single-cause claim. The release attributes the Adjusted EBITDA gain to "improved transaction margins, favorable business mix, and operating leverage". It credits RSCG's direct-profit gain partly to "channel optimization and improved recovery from an expanded buyer base". The consolidated consignment share moved only from 82.5% to 83.1%. A related case is thesis.body: "GAAP net income rose 41% ... and the release attributes the margin gain to asset-light consignment growth and operating leverage". It omits that the release says the prior-year quarter carried non-recurring business realignment expenses, which lift the 41%.
findings.fix: Say consignment mix is one of three drivers the release names, alongside transaction margins and operating leverage. Where the 41% GAAP net income figure is used, note the prior-year realignment base effect once.

findings.quote: We would turn more constructive on a pullback toward the low end of our range
findings.issue: Incoherent with the calls. The target low is $44, above the $43.23 current price, so a "pullback toward the low end" would be a rise. The whole $44–$52 band sits above the price on a HOLD. scenarioCommentary says the band "brackets the Base case" but never explains a HOLD whose target range starts above spot.
findings.fix: Give the entry level as a price below spot that the surface supports, or rephrase. Add one sentence in scenarioCommentary on why a band entirely above the price still gives a HOLD: an expected upside of about 8% against a roughly 21% Bear drawdown.

findings.quote: The counter-case is that cash conversion has trended down even as revenue grew
findings.issue: The series does not show a trend. FCF margin went 23.3%, 13.1%, 13.2%, 16.9%, 12.4%. It fell in FY22, rose in FY23 and FY24, then fell in FY25. "Trended down" overstates a single-year drop from FY24.
findings.fix: Say FCF margin fell to 12.4% in FY25 from 16.9% in FY24, after recovering from the FY22 low. Keep the cash-tax point as the forward risk.

findings.quote: The same proxy says 75% of the board as of that date, are independent under Nasdaq standards.
findings.issue: Dating and grammar. "The same proxy" and "that date" point back to a different field (leadership) that the reader may not have just read. The sentence carries no date of its own, and the stray comma breaks it. The board composition is as of the DEF 14A dated January 16, 2026, more than eight months before this report, so the date changes what the figure means.
findings.fix: Date it in place: "The DEF 14A dated January 16, 2026 says six of the directors, 75% of the board at that date, are independent under Nasdaq standards." Then read what a 75% independent majority with a combined Chairman and CEO lets outside holders do.

findings.quote: The financial data in this report treats the company as a single consolidated unit.
findings.issue: Source disagreement handled twice and incompletely. The same note is repeated in businessMoat.segments[0].body: "The financial data treats the company as one unit, and FY25 revenue of $476.7M is shown as a single consolidated total. The 10-Q, however, reports three segments". The third source, the company description (bigdata tearsheet, which says "four segments: GovDeals, Retail Supply Chain Group (RSCG), Capital Assets Group (CAG), and Machinio"), is silently dropped.
findings.fix: Note the disagreement once, in businessMoat.segments: vendor single segment, tearsheet four, 10-Q three reportable plus Machinio & Software Solutions. Say you used the 10-Q. Cut the sentence from companyOverview.

findings.quote: Auction participants fell 5% in the fiscal third quarter, per the release.
findings.issue: Cross-section repetition of one claim. The auction-participant decline is told with figures in businessMoat.moatFactors[0].body ("auction participants fell 5% in the fiscal third quarter even as completed transactions rose 17%"), growth.points[2] ("Completed transactions rose 17% in the fiscal third quarter while auction participants fell 5%") and risks.idiosyncratic[1] (quoted). It is retold in words in thesis.body ("Growth in auction participants turned negative"), management.leadership ("The weak spot is the decline in auction participants"), businessMoat.durability ("buyer participation fell in the latest quarter"), valuation.scenarioCommentary ("a stall in buyer activity") and finalRecommendation.body[1] ("evidence that auction participation is growing again").
findings.fix: Argue it once, in growth.points[2] or risks.idiosyncratic[1], with the figures and the definition. Elsewhere refer back in words without the 5% and 17%. Drop it from leadership and durability, or make it a short pointer there.

findings.quote: At $43.23 the stock sits close to its 52-week high of $45.00 and trades on 42.4x trailing earnings, while the two covering analysts' targets span only $50.00–$52.00.
findings.issue: Paraphrase repetition of the price-and-valuation claim. Near the 52-week high also appears in thesis.body ("trades near the top of its 52-week range") and finalRecommendation.body[0] ("The share price, close to the 52-week high, already reflects that progress"). 42.4x is repeated in multiplesCommentary. The $50.00–$52.00 band appears in analystCommentary, multiplesCommentary and scenarios[0].driver. $231.1 million with zero financial debt appears in analystCommentary, thesis.body ("Cash of $231.1 million with no financial debt") and balanceCommentary. The HOLD sentence is nearly identical in thesis.body ("We rate the shares HOLD with a target range of $44 to $52.") and finalRecommendation.body[0] ("We rate Liquidity Services HOLD with a target range of $44 to $52.").
findings.fix: Keep each figure in the section that argues it: valuation for the multiples and Street band, balanceCommentary for the cash. In analystCommentary and thesis, point in words. Rewrite one of the two HOLD sentences so no sentence appears in two sections.
findings.note: Figures are now consolidated and the HOLD sentence is no longer duplicated, but the price claim is still repeated in near-identical words: meta.subtitle ("the share price already reflects much of it"), thesis.body ("the share price already reflects much of the improvement") and finalRecommendation.body[0] ("the share price already reflects that progress"), with analystCommentary adding "The problem is price, not quality." Keep it once in the summary; let finalRecommendation conclude in different terms.

findings.quote: Execution in the fiscal third quarter was strong on profit, with Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA up 30% per the release.
findings.issue: Repetition. The 30% Adjusted EBITDA growth is already given in analystCommentary and retold in incomeCommentary ("Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA each growing several times faster than revenue"). The leadership paragraph is otherwise a list of names from the proxy, with no view on what the team's tenure or structure means for holders (rubric 4).
findings.fix: Drop the EBITDA figure here. Use the space for a view the reader can act on, for example the Chairman and CEO's 91% variable pay or the reliance on a combined Chairman and CEO, without restating governance.

findings.quote: The weak spot is the decline in auction participants, which management did not address in the release excerpt.
findings.issue: Misses the source's own framing. The release headline is "Share Expansion, Platform Efficiencies and Strong Buyer Participation Drive Profitable Growth", and the CEO cites "buyer liquidity". Management did address buyer participation and called it strong, in the same release that shows participants down 5%. That tension is the point, and quoting it would strengthen the paragraph.
findings.fix: Quote the headline's "Strong Buyer Participation" against the 5% decline in auction participants, once, wherever you argue the participation point (see the repetition finding).

findings.quote: Bill Angrick is Chairman and CEO, per the DEF 14A dated January 16, 2026
findings.issue: The proxy names him "William P. Angrick, III", Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. "Bill Angrick" is the earnings release's form. Pairing that name with the DEF 14A attaches the release's phrasing to the proxy.
findings.fix: Use "William P. Angrick, III" when citing the proxy. If you use "Bill Angrick", attribute it to the release.

findings.quote: Further gains in RSCG direct profit from the consignment and sell-in-place programs discussed under Financials.
findings.issue: Dead pointer. The Financials section mentions RSCG direct profit but never discusses consignment or sell-in-place programs. That discussion is in businessMoat.segments[0].body and risks.idiosyncratic[2].
findings.fix: Point to Business & Moat, or carry the sell-in-place mechanism in the section named.

findings.quote: the MD&A refers to an acquisition in GovDeals without detail in the excerpt
findings.issue: The MD&A excerpt only cross-refers to "Note 3 - Acquisitions" after describing the GovDeals marketplaces. It does not refer to "an acquisition". The characterization goes beyond the text.
findings.fix: Say the MD&A cross-references an acquisitions note for GovDeals that is not in the excerpt, or drop the clause.

findings.quote: the vendor rounds annual capital expenditure to zero in billions throughout the five-year table
findings.issue: The surface carries the precise figure: the highlight cell capexLatestFY gives FY25 Capital Expenditure = -$7.8M. The sentence implies capex is unquantifiable when it is on the page.
findings.fix: Quote FY25 capital expenditure of $7.8M and drop the rounding remark.

findings.quote: Our view:
findings.issue: Verbal tics. "Our view:" or "Our view is" opens the closing sentence in incomeCommentary, capitalAllocation and multiplesCommentary. "per the release" appears in businessMoat.moatFactors[0] (as "the release shows"), growth.points[2], management.leadership (twice), risks.idiosyncratic[1] and risks.idiosyncratic[2]. Both go past the point of notice.
findings.fix: Vary the closers, or let the final sentence carry the view without a label. Attribute to the release once per section.

findings.quote: That margin fell from 16.9% in FY24, after recovering from a low of 13.1% in FY22.
findings.issue: Misstates the series. FCF margin was 23.3%, 13.1%, 13.2%, 16.9%, 12.4%, so FY25's 12.4% is the lowest of the five years, below the FY22 figure the sentence calls "a low". This rewrite (in response to F-11) hides the most bearish reading the table supports. The counter-case sentence that follows ("conversion slipped in FY25") understates it for the same reason.
findings.fix: Say FCF margin fell to 12.4% in FY25 from 16.9% in FY24, the lowest of the five years shown, below the 13.1% of FY22. Let the counter-case rest on that.

findings.quote: The release credits the profit gain to three things: improved transaction margins, favorable business mix and operating leverage.
findings.issue: The rewrite created new paraphrase repetition. (1) The three-driver attribution is in meta.subtitle, analystCommentary (quoted) and thesis.body ("which the release puts down to transaction margins, business mix and operating leverage"). (2) The small consignment shift is argued in analystCommentary ("its share of GMV moved only slightly, so it is not the whole explanation") and again in financials.incomeCommentary ("83.1% of GMV ... against 82.5% a year earlier, a small shift"). (3) The same 9.0% TTM against 10.9% latest-quarter operating margin comparison appears in both financials.incomeCommentary and valuation.multiplesCommentary.
findings.fix: Make each claim once. Keep the three drivers in analystCommentary or thesis, not both. Argue the consignment-shift size only in incomeCommentary. In multiplesCommentary, refer back to Financials in words ("margins below the current run-rate, see Financials") instead of restating 9.0% and 10.9%.
